definition: Michel Anne Frederic DeGraff (born 1963) is a Haitian creolist and a professor at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT).
details: His scholarship focuses on Creole studies and the role of language and linguistics for decolonization and liberation. He has advocated for the recognition of Haitian Creole as a full-fledged language.

explainer.lead: Michel DeGraff is a Haitian creolist (born 1963). His work spans creolistics.

contributions.name: He developed an interest in linguistics during an internship at Bell Labs in New Jersey in 1985, as a Summer Intern at AT&T Bell Laboratories' Linguistics and Artificial Intelligence department.

timeline.what: DeGraff moved to New York in 1982 and enrolled in City College of New York, where he studied computer science.
Doctor of Philosophy, University of Pennsylvania
In 2022, DeGraff was elected as a fellow of the Linguistic Society of America.
In 2023, DeGraff came into conflict with the MIT administration as a result of his publicly espoused political views.
